motivation: W-R10 falsified temporal-order identifiability of an unordered anchor scorer. Test fixed-width trainable temporal representations rather than continuing static scoring.
hypothesis: With identical 16-feature capacity and supervised budget, position-sensitive or transition-sensitive representations can learn order changes from development tail reversal and generalize to an unseen tail-rotation transformation; a histogram cannot.
freeze: Commit this preregistration before script installation or first experimental execution. No tuning after heldout observations, including thresholds, width, epochs, update rule, feature maps, or learning rate.
data: Exact inherited W-R9 16-step four-channel synthetic generator, nine entities per seed. Positive pairs are identical temporal sequences; negative pairs preserve the anchor and multiset while changing their tail.
candidate_feature_maps: bag-of-rows: 16-bin histogram of first channel modulo 16
transition: 16 circular first-channel transition increments modulo 256
learner: Same deterministic 16-dimensional perceptron with bias, zero-initialized weights, 32 ordered epochs, learning rate 0.1, update if signed margin <=0. Includes exactly one positive and one negative per entity/seed during training.
heldout_metric: Balanced positive and negative accuracy and confusion counts on disjoint heldout seeds, including full per-seed/per-model outcomes. No training or adjustment on heldout records.
classification: ORDER_MODEL_TRANSFER if position and transition both achieve >=0.85 heldout balanced accuracy and histogram <=0.55; PARTIAL_TRANSFER if any temporal model exceeds histogram; otherwise NEGATIVE_TRANSFER. INVALID for data identity or label split failures.
validation: Exact parent/predecessor/source Git blobs, deterministic double invocation, input invariants, frozen original artifact, and one full project regression.
claim_limit: Tiny supervised synthetic representation pilot only; not raw natural language understanding, general reasoning, or accepted-reference promotion.
